glosses: A cast-iron component used on railways to support bullhead rails and secure them to the sleepers.

examples.text: The wooden or steel keys used to secure bull-head rails in their chairs are usually driven in the direction of the traffic, so that the effects of rail-creep may be made use of to wedge the keys more firmly, rather than to encourage them to drop out.

glosses: One of two possible conformers of cyclohexane rings (the other being boat), shaped roughly like a chair.
Ellipsis of electric chair (“device used for performing execution”).

examples.text: The court will show no mercy; if he gets convicted, it's the chair for him.
"It was me. And I'm glad, damned glad, I didn't croak him. With this slick guy after me, it would be me for the chair."
'All for a pig of a man who should have gone to the chair.'
Believe it or not, it only looked like I was trying to send you to the chair.
"Scoleri Brothers!" "Friends of yours?" "I tried them for murder! Gave them the chair!"
I hope you die in prison as well — and if this was a death penalty state you'd be getting the chair.

glosses: A distinguished professorship at a university.

examples.text: In 1928 [Martin] Heidegger succeeded [Edmund] Husserl to take a chair at Freiburg […]

glosses: A vehicle for one person; either a sedan borne upon poles, or a two-wheeled carriage drawn by one horse; a gig.

examples.text: Enter Mortimer, brought in a Chayre, and Iaylors.
She always leaves her Chair at the milliner's in the next Street.

Think what an equipage thou haſt in air,
 And view with ſcorn two pages and a chair.

The chairs came at the appointed hour, and Ethel could not but be amused at the glimpses she had of the park along which they were carried; although haunted by misgivings as to the judiciousness of their destination. They were set down in a hall of large dimensions, hung round with portraits, and filled with servants, who had more the air of guards.

glosses: The seat or office of a person in authority, such as a judge or bishop.
An assigned position in a beauty salon or barbershop.

examples.text: Melinda has the best chair in the salon.

glosses: To act as chairperson at; to preside over.

examples.text: Bob will chair tomorrow's meeting.

Greenwood told RAIL she was disappointed that Parliamentary rules prevented her from chairing the TSC [Transport Select Committee] beyond last December's General Election, [...] She added: "I'm gutted I'm no longer able to chair the committee, I'm not going to lie. But I know it's in good hands and I'm still able to play my part as a member in the work we're doing.

glosses: To carry in a seated position upon one's shoulders, especially in celebration or victory.

examples.text:
The time you won your town the race
We chaired you through the marketplace.

glosses: To award a chair to (a winning poet) at a Welsh eisteddfod.

examples.text: The poet was chaired at the national Eisteddfod.
